newsitem.title: USA: U.S. PRODUCTS OUTLOOK - weather, stocks stir bears.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PRODUCTS OUTLOOK - weather, stocks stir bears.

text.p: Mild weather and waning demand will weigh bearishly on U.S. spot distillates this week, with gasoline seen under downward pressure also from a rapid build in inventories in the past month, traders and analysts said.

Forecasts of temperatures at least ten degrees above normal in both the Northeast and Midwest for most of the week loom unfavorably for heating oil prices, said Stephen Platt, a Dean Witter senior energy analyst.
"Mild weather is pressuring the market, increasing recognition that we're moving out of winter," he said, helping drive March NYMEX values sharply lower by midday Monday.

"The longer you don't have cold temperatures, the less pressure people will feel to restock before winter ends. Most people are probably content with their supplies, and that's removing support," he said.
Another negative factor, he said, is the trend of maintenance turnarounds coming to a close at many Gulf refineries, restoring downed units back to service.
Star Enterprise said last week it would return a 35,000 barrel per day heavy oil unit at its refinery in Convent, Louisiana. The unit was shut December 4 after a fire.

The unit's return helped soften differentials on Gulf low sulfur diesel, which firmed a full five cents a gallon earlier in the week on tight supply and short-covering by traders. Star is a 50-50 joint venture between Texaco and Saudi Aramco.
"The bias on products overall is to the downside," Platt said, abetted by American Petroleum Institute estimates of a 9.7 million barrel build in U.S. crude oil stocks in the past two weeks.
Likewise, he said gasoline stocks have jumped by 8 million barrels in the past four weeks, compared with a mere 2.2 million barrel build during the same period last year.

Although total U.S. gasoline stocks stand 3.4 million barrels below 1996, Platt said the recent surge in crude supplies -- coupled with completion of refinery turnarounds -- should keep the gasoline build going in weeks ahead.

In the Midwest, unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel basis was expected to remain strong through the expiration of the underlying March futures contracts on spot buying ahead of spring maintenance turnarounds at regional refineries.
"Basis should remain strong through the March expiry. After that, distillate should be steady but gasoline could go lower," one Group Three trader said.
Jet/kero basis was expected to remain steady this week after making a steady climb through turbulence caused by a looming strike deadline faced by American Airlines and its pilots union.
President Bill Clinton over the weekend imposed a 60-day cooling off period that averted a shutdown of the airline, which operates one of its three hubs in Chicago.
